title: Galangin enhances skin flap survival by inhibiting ferroptosis via SIRT1-mediated FOXO1 deacetylation.
authors: Yang, Jialong; Wang, An; Qi, Zhengyang; Xu, Panshen; Pan, Hebin; Song, Weilong; Wang, Kaitao; Lin, Dingsheng
journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然黄酮Galangin通过SIRT1/FOXO1通路抑制铁死亡促进皮瓣存活，属于细胞与动物实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Skin flap necrosis due to ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury remains a major obstacle in plastic and reconstructive surgery. Galangin (Gal) is a natural flavonoid with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; its effect on ischemic flap necrosis remains unclear. METHODS: Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict the interaction between Gal and SIRT1. In vitro, human umbilical vein endothelial cells were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion to simulate I/R injury, and subsequent assessments of cell viability and ferroptosis were performed. The SIRT1 inhibitor EX527 and the ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1 were used to verify the ferroptosis-related mechanisms. In vivo, a modified McFarlane skin flap model was created in rats. Gal-treated groups were compared to a control group to evaluate flap survival, blood perfusion, histological changes, and the expression of key proteins in the SIRT1/FOXO1 pathway. RESULTS: In vitro, Gal protected HUVECs by suppressing ferroptosis. Mechanistically, Gal upregulated SIRT1, promoted FOXO1 deacetylation, increased expression of downstream proteins and inhibited lipid peroxidation. These protective effects were diminished by SIRT1 inhibition. In vivo, Gal treatment significantly increased flap survival area and blood perfusion in a dose-dependent manner. It also suppressed neutrophil infiltration, reduced MDA levels, increased SOD activity, and inhibited pro-inflammatory cytokines and activate anti-ferroptosis proteins. CONCLUSIONS: Gal enhances skin flap survival by suppressing ferroptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation via activation of the SIRT1/FOXO1 pathway.
abstract_zh: 背景：缺血再灌注（I/R）损伤导致的皮瓣坏死仍是整形与重建外科中的主要挑战。高良姜素（Galangin, Gal）是一种天然黄酮类化合物，具有强效抗氧化和抗炎特性；其对缺血性皮瓣坏死的作用尚不明确。方法：采用网络药理学和分子对接预测Gal与SIRT1之间的相互作用。体外实验中，对人脐静脉内皮细胞进行氧糖剥夺/再灌注以模拟I/R损伤，随后评估细胞活力和铁死亡。使用SIRT1抑制剂EX527和铁死亡抑制剂Ferrostatin-1验证铁死亡相关机制。体内实验中，在大鼠中建立改良McFarlane皮瓣模型。将Gal处理组与对照组比较，评估皮瓣存活率、血液灌注、组织学变化以及SIRT1/FOXO1通路关键蛋白的表达。结果：体外实验中，Gal通过抑制铁死亡保护HUVECs。机制上，Gal上调SIRT1，促进FOXO1去乙酰化，增加下游蛋白表达并抑制脂质过氧化。这些保护效应在SIRT1抑制后减弱。体内实验中，Gal处理以剂量依赖性方式显著增加皮瓣存活面积和血液灌注，同时抑制中性粒细胞浸润、降低MDA水平、增加SOD活性，并抑制促炎细胞因子和激活抗铁死亡蛋白。结论：Gal通过激活SIRT1/FOXO1通路抑制铁死亡、氧化应激和炎症，从而增强皮瓣存活。
